our_title: Maximum-degree ordering condition declared double but points at a Gnum
ran: gcc ASan/UBSan 32-bit, repro/GRA-06/order.c: `./order '/(mdeg>3)?s;'` -> 'parser.c:437:38: runtime error: load of misaligned address ... for type double, which requires 8 byte alignment' (stratTestEval reads 8 bytes from the 4-byte degrmax); patched: ret=0 invalid=0, mdeg compares the true max degree. 64-bit (build64) patched also clean.
severity_note: Matches review: wrong/out-of-bounds read of a strategy condition; reachable from any user ordering strategy string, but only mis-evaluates a condition (no write).
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/hgraph_order_st.c:231; hdgraph_order_st.c:131; hmesh_order_st.c:207 (table entries); read at parser.c:437
evidence: hgraph_order_st.c:231 `{ STRATNODECOND, STRATPARAMDOUBLE, "mdeg", (byte *) &hgraphorderstgraphdummy, (byte *) &hgraphorderstgraphdummy.s.degrmax, NULL }` with s.degrmax a Gnum; parser.c:437 `evalptr->data.val.valdbl = *((double *) ((byte *) dataptr + testptr->data.var.dataoft));`.
review_accuracy: accurate; fix 'declare mdeg as STRATPARAMINT' is correct. The review cites only hgraph_order_st.c; the same table bug exists in the distributed (hdgraph) and mesh (hmesh) orderings.
first_pass_critique: Correct status/evidence. Its preferred diff bundled the GRA-06 else-branch hunk into the GRA-13 diff (two distinct defects); split here. It missed the hdgraph and hmesh twins.

fix_options.label: Declare mdeg as STRATPARAMINT
fix_options.summary: Match the other integer conditions (vert/edge/load/levl) in all three ordering tables.
fix_options.tested: 32-bit and 64-bit ASan/UBSan; repro passes; check_strat_seq, check_scotch_graph_order, check_prog_gord/mord pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: mdeg is now an integer comparison (consistent with the other graph metrics); a fractional threshold such as mdeg>3.5 is promoted per stratTestEvalCast, as for vert/edge.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Trivial type correction matching every sibling entry; cf. commit 813ef60 'Bugfix: variable type [report R. Perry]'.

fix_options.label: Add a double mirror field
fix_options.summary: Keep STRATPARAMDOUBLE and store a double copy of the max degree in the dummy struct.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Structural change for a trivial variable; only justified for fractional thresholds, which the integer form already supports via promotion.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He would not add a field where a type fix suffices.

notes: One commit fixes all three tables (sequential graph, distributed graph, mesh).

our_title: Nested-dissection ordering with unset osq parameter dereferences a NULL strategy
ran: mpirun -np 3 asan/bin/dgord m16x16.grf /dev/null -o'n{sep=d{pass=3},ole=s,ose=s}' -> 'WARNING: ... strategy parameter "osq" of method "n" not set' then 'hgraph_order_st.c:276:18: runtime error: member access within null pointer of type const struct Strat' and SIGSEGV. After rebuilding libscotch with G04 patch 0009 (osq default = &stratdummy): rc=0, no warning, no crash.
severity_note: Reachable only via a user strategy that omits the osq parameter of method n; the parser already warns.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/hdgraph_order_st.c default table (osq NULL); crash via hdgraphOrderSq2 reaching the n method; parser_yy.y:314 only warns.
evidence: Pristine hdgraphorderstdefaultnd = { { &stratdummy, &stratdummy, &stratdummy } } (three fields for sep/ole/ose, osq left NULL).
review_accuracy: n/a (PS-* found by the first pass).
first_pass_critique: Accurate. Its option A ('reject at parse time') and option B ('guard at use') are both superseded: G04 adopted the maintainer's own idiom of a &stratdummy default for every strategy parameter (G04 patches/0009), which this group is based on, fixing PS-DMO-2 without a new idiom.

fix_options.label: Set &stratdummy default for osq (G04 0009)
fix_options.summary: Add the missing fourth &stratdummy to hdgraphorderstdefaultnd (and the b/bd org defaults), so an unset strategy parameter is the empty strategy, as elsewhere.
fix_options.tested: dgord reproducer passes against the rebuilt library; check_strat_par passes.
fix_options.tradeoffs: None beyond G04's series; consistent with every other default table.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: It is literally the pattern the maintainer uses for all other method parameters.

notes: Fixed by G04's series (patches/0009), on which this group's branch is based; no additional patch from G05. The crash site quoted by the first pass (hgraph_order_st.c:276) is the generic n-method dispatch reached from the distributed ordering.

our_title: Else-less false conditional ordering strategy leaves the permutation unset
ran: repro/GRA-06/order.c 32-bit ASan: `./order '/(vert>1000)?s;'` -> 'AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4 ... orderPeri order.c:170 <- SCOTCH_graphOrderComputeList' (unset peritab indexed by caller sentinel); patched: ret=0 peri[0]=0 invalid=0. 64-bit also clean.
severity_note: Agrees with review: a public ordering call returns success with an unwritten permutation, which the caller then uses (out-of-bounds write) -> memory corruption.
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/hgraph_order_st.c:293-296 (STRATNODECOND else branch); twins hdgraph_order_st.c:199-202, hmesh_order_st.c:273-276
evidence: hgraph_order_st.c:293 `else { if (straptr->data.conddat.stratab[1] != NULL) o = hgraphOrderSt (...stratab[1]); }` -- no else, o stays 0 with nothing written; the STRATNODEEMPTY case just above calls hgraphOrderSi.
review_accuracy: accurate, including the mechanism (orderPeri writes permtab[sentinel]) and the suggested fix (call hgraphOrderSi when stratab[1]==NULL). Review's note about the SCOTCH_DEBUG '&&' is cosmetic and not touched.
first_pass_critique: Right status and fix. It only patched hgraph_order_st.c and folded the GRA-13 table change into the same diff; here the distributed and mesh twins are also fixed and the two defects are separate commits.

fix_options.label: Apply the identity ordering in the else-less case
fix_options.summary: Call *OrderSi when stratab[1]==NULL, mirroring the STRATNODEEMPTY case.
fix_options.tested: 32/64-bit ASan; repro passes; check_scotch_graph_order, check_prog_gord, check_prog_mord pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Produces the identity (graph-order) ordering for the unmatched case; pure addition; precedent: STRATNODEEMPTY in the same routines.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Same hgraphOrderSi call the empty-strategy case already uses; a repair, not a rejection, which ordering needs.

fix_options.label: Reject else-less conditional ordering strategies
fix_options.tradeoffs: Surfaces the mistake but breaks user strategies that omit the else (a documented no-op for mapping/separation); ordering uniquely needs a result.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He treats else-less COND as a no-op elsewhere, so he would repair, not reject.

notes: Same family as G04 PS2-G04-strategy-parser-3: both resolve 'missing strategy -> crash' by the maintainer's guard-at-use idiom (empty/identity strategy), not by a new parser rejection. Consistent across all *_st.c.

our_title: k-way FM fallback strategy leaked and its result unchecked
ran: Verified the defect site and that G13's patches/0006 (GRA-02) rewrites exactly this block: stratInit NULL-checked, kgraphMapSt result captured and propagated, stratExit added, error paths free comploadmax. G13 ran it under LeakSanitizer (fallback frames gone) and check_scotch_graph_map/order.
read_only: Did not re-run the leak harness; relied on reading G13's patch 0006 and SUMMARY and on building the covered block.
severity_note: Agrees: a small leaked strategy tree plus an ignored return on an internal fallback path; same rating as the review.
evidence: Pristine: `strat = stratInit (&kgraphmapststratab, "r{sep=h{pass=10}}"); kgraphMapSt (grafptr, strat);` -- no NULL check, no stratExit, return dropped.
first_pass_critique: Correct; its preferred diff is the same change G13 committed for GRA-02.

fix_options.label: Check NULL, run, stratExit, propagate (G13 patches/0006)
fix_options.summary: stratInit NULL check; capture and propagate kgraphMapSt result; stratExit after use; free on error paths.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Parses the small string on each fallback (already the case).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Committed in G13's GRA-02 series, which owns kgraph_map_fm.c.

notes: Fully covered by G13's GRA-02 commit (kgraph_map_fm.c, not a G05 file); no separate G05 patch. Route alongside G13's series.

our_title: Strategy builders format imbalance ratios into small stack buffers unbounded
ran: repro/API-07/sb.c, sbpt.c (32/64-bit ASan): `./sb 1e300` -> 'AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 309 ... sprintf' in SCOTCH_stratGraphMapBuild/...ClusterBuild/...PartOvlBuild/...OrderBuild/...MeshOrderBuild and the PT-Scotch builders; `1e30` overflows the 32-byte buffers (size 39). Patched: all of 1e300/1e30/nan/inf/-0.5 return 1, no ASan error; 0.05 returns 0. check_strat_seq/par pass with new cases.
severity_note: Raised from the review's medium: an attacker-free stack-buffer-overflow of 300+ bytes reachable directly from a public API argument (balrat), and from the common DBL_MAX 'no constraint' sentinel.
evidence: e.g. library_graph_part_ovl.c:169 `sprintf (kbaltab, "%lf", balrat);` with `char kbaltab[64];` -- '%lf' of 1e300 is ~316 chars.
review_accuracy: accurate on mechanism, sites and size 309. Its '%g' suggestion changes the saved strategy text; 'reject non-finite' is adopted. First-pass claim that the FLOAT lexer has no sign so negatives already fail is WRONG: `SCOTCH_stratGraphMapBuild(&s,...,-0.5)` returns 0 on pristine (VALSDOUBLE accepts a leading sign), so negatives were silently accepted.
first_pass_critique: Its option 1 (bounded snprintf keeping %lf) is the core of the chosen fix, but it did not reject non-finite or negative ratios and its note that negatives already fail in the parser is incorrect (verified -0.5 accepted). The chosen fix adds the isfinite/negative guard and covers all 8 builders and the twins and adds tests.

fix_options.label: Reject non-finite/negative + bounded snprintf (keep %lf)
fix_options.summary: Guard each builder's ratio(s) with !isfinite/<0, convert with snprintf(sizeof) and return 1 on truncation; valid ratios keep their exact %lf text.
fix_options.tested: 32/64-bit ASan sb.c/sbpt.c; check_strat_seq/par (new rejection cases); check_scotch_graph_map/order/part_ovl, check_prog_gmap/gord/mord, dgpart.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Behaviour change only for non-finite/negative and for finite values too large to fit (previously stack smash, now error 1). Output byte-identical for valid ratios.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches the errorPrint+return(1) guard style (cf. b10825d) and the tools' own `-b` validation (dgmap.c rejects <0/>1); keeps %lf so SCOTCH_stratSave golden text is unchanged.

fix_options.label: Format with %.15g and validate
fix_options.tradeoffs: Cannot overflow but changes saved strategy text (0.05 vs 0.050000), visible through SCOTCH_stratSave and golden tests.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He keeps the %lf textual form, so %g would churn saved strategies.

fix_options.label: Enlarge the buffers to 320
fix_options.tradeoffs: Zero behaviour change but wastes stack and leaves sprintf and the 8192 bufftab exposed to ~10 copies of 316-char numbers.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He bounds output, he does not inflate buffers.

test_added: src/check/test_strat_seq.c and test_strat_par.c: a loop rejecting NaN, a negative and 1e300 for every builder
notes: Locale note (unaddressed, pre-existing): %lf is locale-dependent (decimal comma) while the parser uses atof; out of scope for this crash fix. 1e30 remains accepted by the 64-byte-buffer builders (fits, finite) and rejected by the 32-byte ones; no overflow either way.

our_title: Public wrappers ignore their own Init result; coarsen returns 1 not 2 on context failure
ran: repro/API-23 (plain non-ASan build + malloc interposer failing the N-th alloc): SCOTCH_FAIL_AT=3 (graphMapInit part-array alloc) -> pristine 'SCOTCH_graphMapInit: out of memory' then SIGSEGV (rc=139); patched returns 1 (rc=1). graphCoarsen 1->2 change verified by source and doc (s_l.tex states 2 on error; dgraph twin already returns 2).
read_only: The graphCoarsen/CoarsenMatch context-init failure path (1->2) was source/doc-verified, not runtime-forced.
severity_note: Agrees with review: OOM-only NULL dereference (nondeterministic crash) plus a return-code inconsistency; most Init routines can only fail on allocation.
evidence: library_graph_map.c:411 `SCOTCH_graphMapInit (grafptr, &mappdat, archptr, parttab);` result dropped, then Compute runs with a possibly-unallocated part array; library_arch_build.c:131 assigns stratInit() result and dereferences `bipstratptr->tablptr` unconditionally; library_graph_coarsen.c:100 `return (1);` on context failure while the routine documents 2.
review_accuracy: accurate; most Init functions fail only on OOM, hence low. The fix 'check every Init result and return documented codes' is correct.
first_pass_critique: Correct, but method was source-read and 'needs: alloc-injection'; settled here by a malloc interposer that reproduces the SEGV on pristine and the clean return on patched. First pass did not mention the SCOTCH_dgraphMap twin, fixed here too.

fix_options.label: Check each Init result and return documented codes
fix_options.summary: Return the error when *Init fails (as SCOTCH_graphOrder already does); check stratInit in archBuild0; return 2 from graphCoarsen/CoarsenMatch on context failure.
fix_options.tested: malloc-fault repro (SEGV->return 1); 32/64-bit builds 0-warning; check_scotch_graph_map/order, check_scotch_graph_coarsen, check_prog_gmap/gord/mord pass.
fix_options.tradeoffs: graphCoarsen's return on context failure changes from 1 to 2 (the documented error); a caller treating 1 as 'not coarsenable' will notice (now matches the dgraph twin).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Mirrors the existing `if (SCOTCH_graphOrderInit (...) != 0) return (1);` idiom (library_graph_order.c:413) and the dgraph coarsen twin's `return (2)`.

fix_options.label: Make Init infallible
fix_options.summary: Allocate nothing in *Init; defer to Compute.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Changes Init/Exit allocation semantics of the public pair; larger redesign.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Too invasive for an error-handling fix.

notes: Two commits: 0005 fixes the graphCoarsen/CoarsenMatch return code (documented 2), 0006 checks the Init/stratInit results in the mapping and ordering wrappers and archBuild0.

our_title: dgmap/dgpart rebuild the default strategy after parsing, discarding -m
ran: repro/CLI-01 (ASan, mpirun -np 3): `dgpart 9 bump.grf /dev/null -Cd -m'r{sep=q{strat=f}}'` -> pristine completes (0 crashes: -m discarded, default used); patched honours -m and the strategy reaches the mapper (SIGSEGV from the incomplete string). Exclusivity check still fires with -b0.1. dgmap.c is shared by dgmap and dgpart.
severity_note: Agrees: every -m strategy on dgmap/dgpart was silently ignored (wrong result), a public-tool option that never took effect.
evidence: dgmap.c:259 `straptr=&argv[i][2]; SCOTCH_stratExit(&stradat); SCOTCH_stratInit(&stradat); SCOTCH_stratDgraphMap(&stradat,straptr);` then unconditionally at 391 `SCOTCH_stratDgraphClusterBuild/...MapBuild(&stradat,...)`, which frees and reparses the default.
review_accuracy: accurate; line numbers unshifted; suggested guard matches dgord.c/gmap.c. The first-pass caveat (an incomplete user -m now reaches the mapper and crashes in dmapSave) is confirmed and reported as PS2-G05-strategy-tables-api-1.
first_pass_critique: Accurate and thorough (library + tool repro). Confirmed its note that dgord is not affected (it only Builds when straval!=0).

fix_options.label: Guard the default Build with straptr==NULL
fix_options.summary: Build the default strategy only when no -m string was given.
fix_options.tested: repro shows -m now honoured; exclusivity preserved; check_prog_dgpart passes.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Smallest change; users who passed -m (previously ignored) now get it run, which may expose incomplete user strategies.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Matches the `if (straptr != NULL)`/`if (straval != 0)` idioms in gmap.c and dgord.c.

fix_options.label: Defer -m parsing to after the exclusivity check (gmap.c structure)
fix_options.summary: Remember straptr only, then apply -m or Build after the checks; drops the redundant Exit/Init.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Larger diff, same behaviour; mirrors gmap.c more closely.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Also acceptable; the minimal guard is lower risk.

notes: No other tool has the pattern: gmap/gord/dgord/mord only Build when their own -b/-c flag is set and error if -m is also given.
